comment: The eight criteria describe design properties of a component. They do not answer the prior question a finance ministry asks: is society dependent on this function such that public financing, supply-security obligations and holdership should attach? A component can satisfy all eight criteria and still be discretionary, and a function society cannot do without may satisfy none of them.

public.text: The eight criteria describe design properties of a component. They do not answer the prior question a finance ministry asks: is society dependent on this function such that public financing, supply-security obligations and holdership should attach? A component can satisfy all eight criteria and still be discretionary, and a function society cannot do without may satisfy none of them.
public.suggestedRevision: Add a dependency test applied first and cumulatively: (1) irreplaceability - does care delivery or a statutory right stop if this function fails, with no timely alternative route; (2) norm dependence - does its value depend on others using the same rules, so unilateral choices create externalities for third parties; (3) absence of exit - can a participant switch away within a reasonable period without loss of information or continuity. All three yes: infrastructure, warranting holdership, supply security and a tariff. Norm dependence only: standard-setting without a tariff. None: market. The eight design criteria then specify what such a component must look like.
